item.title: iPhone Duo pre-orders open Friday, and repairs won't be cheap
item.description:
Apple's first foldable goes on sale Friday, October 16 at 5 a.m. PT, arriving Friday, October 23. Apple gave customers until 9 p.m. PT Thursday to complete its 'Get Ready' checkout for one-click ordering.

The phone starts at $1,999 and climbs to $3,199 for 2TB — but repair prices may sting more: an inner display fix costs $999, outer display damage $379 (or $509 with back glass). A 'renewable' inner display layer could make upkeep surprisingly affordable, and early Geekbench 7 results show the A20 Pro loses nothing to the thin foldable design, matching iPhone 18 Pro performance.

Meanwhile CEO John Ternus landed on the cover of TIME's Best Inventions of 2026, calling early foldables 'kind of cheap and crappy' and revealing he and five engineers patented foldable concepts back in 2011. Apple execs also pushed back on claims it's 'just using a Samsung display,' describing Samsung as a key supplier of a display Apple designed.

Sources

  • Apple Newsroom: Open up to new possibilities with iPhone Duo
  • MacRumors: Apple Announces Deadline to 'Get Ready' to Pre-Order the iPhone Duo
  • 512 Pixels: The iPhone Duo is Expensive to Repair
  • 9to5Mac: The ‘renewable’ iPhone Duo display layer may help buyers justify the price
  • AppleInsider: iPhone Duo has uncompromised performance, same as iPhone 18 Pro

item.title: Meta and Apple team up to run a 800B-parameter AI model on Mac Studio
item.description:
Meta released Muse Spark Open, which it calls the 'most capable U.S. open-weight model to date': a multimodal large language model with over 800 billion parameters (around 40 billion active per token via mixture-of-experts), built for coding, software engineering, and multi-step tasks.

The surprise is the hardware story. Meta worked directly with Apple to optimize the model for the Mac, and it can run locally on a desktop setup of two 512GB M5 Ultra Mac Studios (or four 256GB machines) using Apple's MLX framework — no cloud required. Mark Zuckerberg publicly thanked John Ternus for the collaboration, and Ternus replied that 'Mac Studio keeps pushing the boundaries of on-device AI.' For developers who want frontier-class open models without a data center, this is a milestone.

Sources

  • MacRumors: Meta and Apple Bring Muse Spark Open AI Model to Mac Studio
  • 9to5Mac: Meta launches new Muse Spark Open model, optimized to run on Mac Studio
  • MacStories: Meta Releases Muse Spark Open, an Over 800 Billion Parameter Model That Can Run Locally on Multiple M5 Ultra Mac Studios

item.title: Apple sets October 28 'launch experience' for touchscreen MacBook Pro and OLED iPad mini
item.description:
Apple has invited selected media to an all-day 'launch experience' in Los Angeles on Wednesday, October 28, covering touchscreen OLED MacBook Pros, a new OLED iPad mini, and M6-equipped Macs — with the MacBook Pros reportedly hitting stores Friday, November 6, backed by a big retail floor reset the night before.

Apple also confirmed the iPad mini itself: its French regulatory site briefly listed an unreleased iPad mini Smart Folio (model A3632), suggesting a redesign current cases won't fit. Mark Gurman says Apple tested both 60Hz and 120Hz ProMotion displays for the mini, final choice unknown. The OLED MacBook Pro is expected with an A20-class chip, landscape camera, and water resistance. On chips: Gurman says Apple is 'pretty much done' with M6 — no M6 Pro, Max, or Ultra — and the OLED MacBook Pro will stick with M5 Pro/Max until M7 arrives in late 2027.

item.title: HomeView's $300+ price draws skepticism as ship times slip
item.description:
Apple's new smart-home hub is getting a rough first reception. Marques Brownlee says he 'cannot figure any group that this is actually ideal for,' arguing the HomeView overlaps too much with the iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, and HomePod without enough 'extra value' — and its lack of an App Store limits what it can do. AppleInsider agrees the $300-and-up device is 'not really clear who it's for.'

Some fine print is fueling the skepticism: the wall-mounted model ships without a power adapter, USB-C cable, or mount, all sold separately. Demand looks healthy anyway — pre-order ship times for HomeView and the new Apple TV 4K have already slipped into late November, past the November 13 availability date. John Gruber did the math: a 128GB Apple TV plus two HomePod minis now costs $600, up from $350 four months ago.

item.title: Apple pledged $25 million to Trump's White House ballroom
item.description:
The Washington Post obtained a donor list showing Apple pledged $25 million toward President Trump's White House ballroom project, making it one of the largest donors alongside Nvidia ($25 million) and the Adelson family. The list totals $333 million in private donations from companies including Microsoft, Comcast, Amazon, Cisco, Meta, T-Mobile, HP, Palantir, Salesforce, and Micron — plus Google, whose contribution came from a lawsuit settlement.

The story's bite is who's on the list and why it was secret: the Post notes previously undisclosed contributors who have benefited from regulatory decisions, government contracts, and in one case a pardon for a family member. The White House has never publicly disclosed the donation amounts, though political giving of this kind typically requires disclosure. The White House declined to comment on individual donors.

Sources

  • 9to5Mac: WaPo: Apple revealed as one of the top donors to Trump’s White House ballroom

item.title: OpenAI vows not to use Apple's trade secrets as injunction looms
item.description:
Apple's July 2026 lawsuit against OpenAI over alleged trade secret theft — files allegedly taken by ex-Apple employees who joined OpenAI — took a sharp turn: after the judge said he was 'highly likely' to grant Apple's injunction, OpenAI volunteered not to use any proprietary Apple information while the case continues, effectively conceding the substance without formally admitting it. Apple has also issued its official response to OpenAI's allegations.

Separately, in a TIME interview, marketing chief Greg Joswiak drew a bright line between Apple Intelligence and the frontier-model world: Apple builds AI for 'everyday people,' not the 'lunatic fringe' of die-hard AI believers in Silicon Valley. He also said Apple doesn't feel threatened by OpenAI's hardware ambitions. It's the clearest statement yet of Apple's AI positioning: modest, personalized, privacy-preserving — and pointedly not chasing the hype cycle.

Sources

  • 9to5Mac: Here’s Apple’s official response to OpenAI’s trade secret theft allegations

item.title: Withings puts Apple Health syncing behind a $100/year paywall for new users
item.description:
Withings, maker of smart scales that measure 60+ biomarkers, has gated one of its most basic features: anyone who created a Withings account on or after October 13, 2026 must pay for Withings+ ($99.50/year in the U.S.) to auto-sync data to third-party apps including Apple Health. Existing accounts are grandfathered in.

The change is striking because Apple Health integration was long advertised as a core feature of Withings products, and free syncing to Apple's Health app is effectively table stakes for health hardware in the Apple ecosystem. The company is betting new buyers won't balk at a subscription costing nearly as much as some of its scales. Expect this to become a cautionary example in 'everything is a subscription' discourse — and a reason to buy health gear from brands that don't ransom your own data back to you.

item.title: Apple closes above $5 trillion for the first time
item.description:
Apple became only the second company ever to close a trading day with a market capitalization above $5 trillion, following Nvidia's milestone last October. The stock finished Wednesday at $342.96, for a valuation of $5.005 trillion. Apple had crossed the $5 trillion line intraday six times before, but this is the first time it held into the close.

The milestone arrives just over a month after John Ternus succeeded Tim Cook as CEO and two days before pre-orders open for the iPhone Duo, Apple's first foldable. Investors appear to be betting that strong iPhone 18 Pro demand and the Duo launch will carry the stock higher, even as Apple fights a bruising trade-secrets battle with OpenAI and races to bring Apple Intelligence to China.

item.title: Apple and OpenAI trade fresh accusations in escalating trade-secrets fight
item.description:
At a court hearing Wednesday, OpenAI voluntarily agreed not to use Apple's alleged trade secrets while the companies' litigation plays out — while simultaneously arguing the shoe is on the other foot. In a new filing, OpenAI says a former employee who joined from Apple, stayed six months, then returned to Apple sent "over a hundred highly confidential files" — including manufacturing data and images of at least one unreleased OpenAI device — to personal accounts, and later presented OpenAI's product plans to Apple's senior leadership. Apple told Reuters it has found no evidence to support the claims.

The tit-for-tat filings mark a sharp escalation. OpenAI even implied Apple's new HomeView may have been influenced by the alleged theft. Expect the forensic investigation at the heart of the case to keep both companies' hardware plans under a microscope for months.

item.title: Apple Intelligence finally heads to China in December — without Siri AI
item.description:
After two years of regulatory wrangling, Apple will bring Apple Intelligence to China in iOS 27.3, expected this December, according to Bloomberg. The launch will cover basic features like photo editing, but Siri AI, Image Playground, and the new Genmoji won't make the cut, and text-generation tools will be limited.

China's strict AI rules required Apple to route its features through local models; the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology recently granted network access permits for Alibaba's Qwen and Tongyi Wanxiang models on the iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, and earlier iPhones. It's a long-overdue unlock of AI features in one of Apple's most important markets — though the trimmed-down version means Chinese users wait longer still for the full Siri AI experience.

item.title: iPhone Duo's first benchmark matches the 18 Pro; repairs could cost up to $1,499
item.description:
Two days before Friday's pre-orders, the iPhone Duo is coming into focus. A Geekbench 7 listing for the foldable (running iOS 27.1) shows single-core ~3,986 and multi-core ~11,067 — squarely in line with the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, as expected from the shared 2nm A20 Pro chip.

The other number to know: Apple posted out-of-warranty repair fees, and they're eye-watering. "Other damage" runs up to $1,499, battery replacement is $229, back glass is $199, and a replacement nano-texture cover layer for the inner display is $49. At equivalent storage the Duo costs $800 more than the iPhone 18 Pro while asking buyers to accept roughly 40 compromises — from camera capabilities to everyday usability — in exchange for the folding 7.6-inch inner display. With a $1,999 starting price, AppleCare+ looks close to mandatory, exactly as Apple intends.

item.title: Apple clears up the Siri AI rollout confusion — original HomePod mini misses out
item.description:
A day after its home-device launch blitz, Apple drew the Siri AI support lines. The original HomePod mini (S5 chip) will not get Siri AI, Apple confirmed, correcting a CNET report that had claimed otherwise. Siri AI ships at launch on November 13 with HomeView and the 4th-gen Apple TV 4K; the 2nd- and 3rd-gen Apple TV 4K get it in tvOS 27.2; and the HomePod mini 2 — shipping October 30 with an S10 chip — won't get Siri AI until a future software update. Two clues on Apple's website suggest the full-size HomePod 2 may eventually join the club, though Apple hasn't confirmed it.

The staggered rollout underscores how deeply the new Siri depends on recent silicon: Siri AI requests involving personal context also require an Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone or iPad. If you're counting on smarter Siri at home, the fine print matters more than the keynote.

item.title: HomeView fallout: FCC filing reveals 2024 testing, $279 repair fee, CarPlay-based app story
item.description:
New details keep surfacing about Apple's $299 HomeView, launching November 13. An FCC filing shows the device was undergoing regulatory testing in October 2024 running what would now be called HomeView software version 18 — the clearest evidence yet that its two-year delay was caused by the Siri AI holdup, resolved only with Siri AI's launch this September.

Apple's specs page lists 15 built-in apps (Home, FaceTime, Music, Intercom, and more) and confirms there's no App Store: third-party support comes via CarPlay-enabled audio and video apps from a paired iPhone — Spotify, YouTube, Netflix, and others can appear if they opt in, plus third-party iPhone widgets work. AppleInsider warns the CarPlay entitlement process, designed for cars, could be a bottleneck for home developers. And the fine print stings: Apple charges a flat $279 to repair a $299 HomeView without AppleCare — 93% of the price of a new one.

item.title: Quick hits: AirTag Silencer pulled, Apple Maps gets Austin, Apple I fetches $1.15M
item.description:
ElevationLab yanked its AirTag Silencer after a backlash over the obvious stalking risk — the accessory that mutes an AirTag's speaker was, critics noted, a gift to anyone misusing trackers. Apple's Pixar-like Detailed City Experience in Apple Maps launched in Austin ahead of the F1 Grand Prix, with custom Circuit of the Americas details — part of Apple's F1 promotional push as holder of the U.S. streaming rights. And the famous "Hatfield" Apple I, signed by Steve Wozniak with a letter from Steve Jobs, sold at Bonhams for $1.15 million, showing the original Apple computer keeps appreciating as a collector's item.

Also worth knowing: the latest HomePods (mini 2 and HomePod 2) can now serve as default system-audio speakers on Macs with Wi-Fi 6E or later, iOS 27 adds 15+ extra-large Home Screen widgets built for the iPhone Duo, and the new Siri Remote's Precision Finding only works with iPhones in the iPhone 17 generation or newer.

item.title: Apple unveils HomeView, its $299 smart home hub
item.description:
Apple finally entered the smart home display race on Tuesday with HomeView, a 7-inch Liquid Retina smart home hub running Siri AI on an A18 chip. Priced at $299, it ships in two configurations — a tabletop model with a domed speaker base and a wall-mount version — and serves as a central dashboard for music, FaceTime calls, calendars, and HomeKit accessories.

The standout trick is personalization: HomeView recognizes up to six household members, unlocking each person's Messages, Calendar, Reminders, and Find My content when it senses they're nearby, without requiring biometrics — it leans on your other Apple devices for authentication. There is no on-device App Store; instead, third-party audio and video apps (Spotify, Audible, and CarPlay-style apps) stream in from a paired iPhone or iPad. Pre-orders are open now, with delivery expected around November 13.

item.title: HomeView's fine print: no EU launch, costly repairs, and adapter not included
item.description:
The HomeView launch came with a stack of caveats. Most notably, it is not launching in the EU — the first time Apple's regulatory clash over the Digital Markets Act has blocked a hardware release, since the device depends on Siri AI, which Apple has kept out of Europe amid DMA disputes.

Other gotchas: the wall-mounted model ships without a power adapter in the box (and needs a compatible one bought separately, including the $59 wall mount itself sold apart); out-of-warranty repairs cost $279 versus $39 with AppleCare+; and HomeView can't natively play Apple TV, Apple Music Classical, audiobooks, or News+ content — those still require an iPhone or iPad. HomeView also lacks VESA mounting holes, limiting third-party wall-mount options at launch.

item.title: New Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini 2 round out the home refresh
item.description:
Alongside HomeView, Apple refreshed the rest of its home lineup. The fourth-generation Apple TV 4K jumps from the A15 to the A19 chip, adds built-in microphones for Siri, Wi-Fi 7, and more storage — but at $299, it doubles the starting price that shocked the Apple press last generation. Four-speaker HomePod surround sound requires the new box, though a new $59 Siri Remote with Find My and Precision Finding works with existing models.

The $149 HomePod mini 2 gets new colors, a faster chip, richer sound, and can serve as a Mac's default speaker — but Siri AI won't be available at its October 30 launch, arriving in a future software update. Generously, Siri AI is coming to older Apple TV 4K models going back to 2021, so existing owners don't need the $299 upgrade for the new assistant.

item.title: Apple partners with LG and Schneider on 'Apple Home Collection' accessories
item.description:
Apple isn't building its own cameras and thermostats — instead it announced the Apple Home Collection, a lineup of smart home accessories developed with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. The range includes a $249.95 LG video doorbell, floodlight camera, thermostats, temperature sensors, and a smart door lock, all designed to be set up with a single tap from an iPhone and controlled through the Home app and Siri.

The strategic angle: camera footage stays private, even from Apple, and everything orbits around HomeView as the control center. But temper expectations on timing — select devices arrive in December, with the rest rolling out through 2027, so the ecosystem is more promise than product for now.

item.title: iOS 27.2 beta 4 drops the Health app redesign, adds monochrome Apple Music icon
item.description:
Apple seeded fourth developer betas of iOS 27.2, iPadOS 27.2, macOS Golden Gate 27.2, watchOS 27.2, and visionOS 27.2 on Tuesday, with public betas following hours later. The headline change is a notable subtraction: the redesigned Health app with Insights and Longevity tabs, tested in earlier betas, is gone from this build — Apple says the redesign won't ship until later in 2026, signaling the 27.2 release is imminent.

Visually, the Apple Music icon goes monochrome — black on white in light mode, white on black in dark mode — with blue accents replacing red inside the app. New AirPods beta firmware also rolled out across Pro 2/3, AirPods 4/5, and Max 2 with no release notes, and second release candidates of macOS Sequoia 15.8.2 and Tahoe 26.7.2 arrived a week after the first.

item.title: Apple fights to overturn the record $5.7B Taction patent verdict
item.description:
Apple is asking a federal judge to throw out the record $5.7 billion verdict it lost in September to Taction Technology, arguing the jury's damages award was "based on guesswork." Taction sued Apple back in April 2021, alleging the Taptic Engine in iPhones and Apple Watches was a reverse-engineered copy of its haptic patents.

In a Tuesday filing, Apple argues not only that it doesn't infringe Taction's patents, but that the damages calculation had no legitimate basis — an aggressive posture aimed at either killing the verdict outright or forcing a massive reduction on appeal. Whatever the judge decides, this is likely to drag on: a verdict this size will almost certainly head to the appeals court either way.

item.title: Judge grants Apple partial discovery win in OpenAI trade secrets case
item.description:
Judge Edward Davila granted Apple some — but not all — of the expedited discovery it requested in its trade secrets lawsuit against OpenAI, io Products, and former Apple employees Tang Yew Tan and Chang Liu. Apple can access testimony from OpenAI employees and select related documents, but the court narrowed the scope of what it must hand over.

Apple alleges the two ex-employees stole trade secrets and IP to benefit OpenAI, including by keeping work-issued devices active after leaving and emailing themselves supplier information. The ruling moves the case forward on Apple's timeline, though the partial grant suggests the judge wants to keep discovery from becoming a fishing expedition. This is one of the highest-stakes talent wars playing out in court right now.

item.title: Everything else Apple has coming in October: iPhone Duo, Oct 27 event, iOS 27.2
item.description:
The home announcements are only the start of a packed October. The iPhone Duo — Apple's first foldable — opens pre-orders October 16 and launches October 23, with a day-one iOS 27.1 update already seeded to handle launch-day bugs. Apple is rumored to hold another event on October 27 covering an OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro, M6 14-inch MacBook Pro, M6 iMac, and OLED iPad mini. Software-wise, iOS/iPadOS/macOS 27.2 are expected by October 30, the same day HomePod mini 2 launches.

Separately, IDC's Q3 numbers show Apple's iPhone shipments in China fell 4.3% year-over-year — but its market share grew as the overall Chinese smartphone market plunged 15.4%, a sign Apple is holding ground in a shrinking market ahead of the foldable launch.

item.title: iPhone hits record Q3 shipment share as the global market plunges
item.description:
The iPhone captured a record Q3 share of global smartphone shipments even as the overall market plunged 20 percent, according to a new report. Counterpoint-style data shows Apple trailing Samsung in absolute shipments but winning share — a premium-market story that keeps playing out in downturns.

Wall Street is split on what comes next: JP Morgan hiked its AAPL price target to $360 while dismissing recent iPhone production-cut reports. Either demand is fine, or the cuts were never real; either way, the analyst community is pricing in a strong holiday quarter.

For Apple, this is about answering the gaming question — the M-series chips are overkill for the mobile game library, and marquee ports like this are how Apple convinces developers the platform is serious.

item.title: Beats x Pokémon Pill speaker, Tim Cook's third China trip, and more
item.description:
Beats and Pokémon teased a special Pikachu-themed Pill speaker collaboration — a nostalgia play aimed squarely at a generation that grew up with both brands. Details are thin, but the teaser confirms it's real.

Meanwhile, Tim Cook visited China for the third time this year, underscoring how central the market and supply chain remain despite geopolitical noise. And in smaller news: Apple launched a special-edition AirPods 5 in India, OLED iPad Mini rumors point to a $200 price bump, and Apple kicked off a "Switch to Safari" campaign arguing you should ditch Chrome.

item.title: Apple vs. Epic flares up again in court
item.description:
The Apple-Epic fight isn't over: a new joint filing shows Epic remains unhappy with Apple "at every turn," and the two sides clashed over document production in the latest App Store court filing. Years after the original verdict, compliance and enforcement are still being litigated.

The stakes are bigger than one case — every skirmish in this saga sets precedent for how app store rules get enforced globally. Expect more rounds.

Sources

  • AppleInsider News: New joint filing shows Epic remains unhappy with Apple at every turn
  • 9to5Mac: Apple and Epic clash over document production in latest App Store court filing

item.title: Apple's smart home hub is called 'HomeView,' ships mid-November in four colors
item.description:
The biggest pre-event leak: Apple's smart-home hub will be called HomeView, ship in mid-November in four colors, and run on an A18 chip, per MacRumors and 9to5Mac. Six Colors confirms the name and frames it as the centerpiece of Tuesday's 'Welcome Home' event.

AppleInsider adds that ADT is rumored to handle installations — a smart move that gives Apple a professional-install story on day one instead of asking the Hub to bootstrap an ecosystem alone. The question hanging over all of it: is this finally Apple's first real smart-home success?

item.title: Apple TV 4K gets A19 chip, easier-to-find Siri Remote, possible built-in mic
item.description:
MacRumors reports the new Apple TV 4K will get an A19 chip and a Siri Remote that's easier to find — likely meaning speaker/UWB tracking. AppleInsider and 9to5Mac add that the box itself might have microphones, and both the Apple TV 4K and HomePod Mini are expected to ship October 30.

MacRumors' roundup collects 16 leaked details across the Apple TV, HomeView, and HomePod Mini. The through-line: Apple is treating the living room as a platform again, not an accessory.

item.title: What to expect at Tuesday's 'Welcome Home' event
item.description:
AppleInsider and The Verge both published event previews ahead of the October 13 'Welcome Home' releases. Expect the HomeView hub, HomePod Mini 2, and Apple TV 4K to headline, with the smart-home angle tying everything together.

TechCrunch asks the sharper question — will HomeView be Apple's first smart-home success? — while Techmeme looks at the broader strategy centered on the hub display. After years of HomeKit half-measures, Tuesday is Apple's put-up-or-shut-up moment in the home.

item.title: iPhone Duo gets huge retail showcases — but supply will be limited
item.description:
MacRumors reports Apple is planning major iPhone Duo retail demo experiences at select stores, with 9to5Mac adding detail on the in-store push. The catch: supply will be limited at launch.

Big experiential retail plus constrained supply is a familiar Apple playbook — it worked for Vision Pro — and suggests the Duo is positioned as a halo product rather than a volume play, at least initially.

item.title: iPad outlook: no new entry-level model until 2027; OLED iPad mini will be pricey
item.description:
AppleInsider and MacRumors report the updated entry-level iPad won't arrive until early 2027 — a long wait that suggests Apple is holding the line on its current lineup through the holidays.

Meanwhile, Bloomberg via 9to5Mac says the OLED iPad mini will be 'significantly more expensive' than the current model. OLED is a real upgrade, but the mini has always sold on value — a big price jump could test that.

item.description:

item.description:
AppleInsider notes Tim Cook is visiting China for the third time in 2026 — a frequency that underscores how critical the market remains amid ongoing supply-chain and regulatory pressures.

Daring Fireball observes Apple only started suggesting iOS 26 users upgrade to 27 three days ago, an unusually quiet rollout for a major release. And in fun news, AppleInsider found a vibe-coded Adobe Creative Suite clone that's 'pretty good' — the vibe-coding era claims another victim.

item.title: Apple's 'Welcome Home' event is Tuesday: Home Hub, HomePod Mini 2, new Apple TV 4K
item.description:
Apple's October 13 'Welcome Home' event is shaping up as the company's biggest smart-home moment in years. MacRumors reports the headliner is an all-new Home Hub — a brand-new device category for Apple, not just another speaker — joined by a HomePod Mini 2 with new features and a long-overdue Apple TV 4K refresh.

Six Colors zooms out to ask whether Apple is 'coming home to stay,' arguing this event signals a serious renewed push into the home after years of half-hearted dabbling with HomeKit. If the Hub lands, it would be Apple's first truly new product category since the Vision Pro — with very different stakes. MacRumors' Top Stories roundup collects everything expected so you can walk into Tuesday fully briefed.

item.title: iPhone 18 Pro orders reportedly cut; iPhone Duo will greet owners by name
item.description:
Supply-chain sources claim Apple has cut iPhone 18 Pro orders 'right on schedule' — a rumor that surfaces nearly every iPhone cycle, usually says more about seasonal production adjustments than actual demand, and should be taken with the usual skepticism until sales data arrives.

More concrete: AppleInsider found that the iPhone Duo will greet some owners by name on first boot, a small personal touch in the setup experience that hints at how Apple is thinking about first-run personalization going forward.

Sources

  • AppleInsider: Right on schedule, sources claim iPhone 18 Pro orders have been cut
  • AppleInsider: iPhone Duo will greet some owners by name on its first boot

item.title: Amazon's Alexa Tablet finally gives the iPad real competition
item.description:
9to5Mac argues Amazon's new Alexa Tablet is the first credible iPad challenger in years — and the threat is real precisely because it doesn't try to beat the iPad at Apple's game. Instead it attacks from below with aggressive pricing and an Alexa-first experience.

No Android tablet has managed sustained pressure on the iPad, but Amazon's content ecosystem and smart-home integration give this one a different angle. If it sells, expect Apple to feel pressure to defend the low end of the lineup rather than ceding it entirely.

item.title: Weekend deals: $430 off MacBook Pro M5 Pro, plus AirPods and accessory sales
item.description:
A strong weekend for Apple deals. AppleInsider spots $430 off the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro, bringing it to $2,069 — one of the steepest discounts on current-gen Pro hardware.

MacRumors rounds up weekend accessory deals spanning TVs, headphones, and smart home gear, while 9to5Mac lists Apple's own weekend sales: AirPods, up to $200 off new Macs, and Apple Watch starting from $41. If you've been waiting on any of these, this is a genuine buy window, not the usual token $20 off.

item.title: Rumor: Apple to announce new partnership with ADT
item.description:
MacRumors reports Apple is set to announce a new partnership with home-security company ADT. Details are thin, but the timing — days before the 'Welcome Home' event — is conspicuous.

An ADT tie-up would give Apple's smart-home push an installed base and professional-monitoring story on day one, rather than asking the Home Hub to bootstrap an ecosystem alone. Expect more partnerships like this if Apple is serious about the home.
